statement: You are given an n × n grid where grid[r][c] is the elevation of cell (r, c). All elevations are distinct.

Rain makes the water level rise: at time t the water is t deep everywhere. You can swim from a cell to the cell directly above, below, left or right of it only when both elevations are at most t, and swimming itself takes no time.
Starting at the top-left cell (0, 0), return the earliest time at which you can reach the bottom-right cell.

examples.explanation: To get past row 1 a route must step on one of 21 to 24, or on the 5 at its right end, and the only way on from that 5 is the 16 below it. Going 0 → … → 5 → 16, then left along row 2, down the left column and right along the bottom row never exceeds 16, so 16 is the answer.
The destination itself has elevation 3, so you cannot be standing on it before time 3, and at time 3 every cell is open.
Going down through the cell of height 2 avoids the 3, so the route 0 → 2 → 1 is open at time 2.

constraints: all values in grid are distinct
